newsitem.title: FRANCE: INSTANT VIEW - New French government ministers.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - New French government ministers.

text.p: Following are financial market analysts' comments after the naming of French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's government ministers on Wednesday.
IAIN LINDSAY, SENIOR BOND ANALYST, CREDIT LYONNAIS
The markets haven't fathomed who these new people are. The personalities being named here don't advance the perception of how the Jospin government will approach policy questions.
Dominique Strauss-Kahn (named finance minister) is a good sort of level-headed Socialist figure which the markets should take comfort from. He's not the sort of guy who would take too many risks.
DOMINIQUE BARBET, HEAD OF RESEARCH, PARIBAS CAPITAL MARKETS

The communists don't have much weight in the government. The important thing is that the key economic portfolios are in safe hands, which appears to be the case. With a government like this there is no reason for markets to fall.
The debt market, which fell today, should rebound higher and PIBOR should continue to climb. The next step will be the first measures of the government and the overall policy statement from Jospin.
HUGUES DE MONTVALON, ECONOMIST, BROKERS ODDO ET CIE

The fact that Martine Aubry, minister for employment and social solidarity, is also the number two in the government shows to which point (Prime Minister Lionel) Jospin is committed to keeping his promises.
The employment minister has in this way precedence over the economy and finance minister. It's a total reversal of the "liberal-interventionist economy" mix of the past 10 years.
We can already start to forget the budget criterion (of three percent of GDP in the Maastricht Treaty).
STEVEN ENGLANDER, INTERNATIONAL ECONOMIST, SMITH BARNEY

At the top there aren't any surprises. Dominique Strauss-Kahn (finance and industry minister) is their spokesman on economics. He's not a free marketeer in the U.S. or U.K. sense, but he has experience and he's viewed as one of the safe hands in the Socialist party.
Strauss-Kahn was adamant that they would go to European Monetary Union on time, but less clear about whether that would be under Jospin's conditions.
(Justice Minister) Elisabeth Guigou had been tipped as European Affairs minister... People will be interested to see if (European Affairs Minister Pierre) Moscovici is as pro-Europe as she was.

This (government list) resolves the question of what role the Communists will play. They have one substantial ministry (transport) and one pro-forma post (youth and sports)...They've done reasonably well.
For the markets, now what's left is to see the programmes and speed at which the ministries will implement them.
MARIE OWENS-THOMSEN, ECONOMIST, DRESDNER KLEINWORT BENSON
The cabinet is perfectly in line with the campaign rhetoric. We have to hope that once they have been in power some time they will prove to be less dangerous than they could be.
You have those streaks in the government which are anti-Maastricht, in favour of increased spending. Obviously these are things to worry about. But the cabinet is no worse than the election results.

There are definitely risks in this government. The apppointment of Strauss-Kahn as finance ministers suggests they are into preserving the French model and not into any major changes of the social system.

The nomination of Communist ministers to relatively minor posts will not be very different than if the party had tried to influence things from parliament without taking part in government so that is in conformity with the markets' preferred solution.
-- Paris Newsroom +331 4221 5452
